amendment: Amendment 2 (2026-11-11) — §3 is withdrawn; this file implements §A2.2's sequential procedure instead
design: Sequential, first match wins. Five personas per condition, one draw each except A0 which is drawn three times interleaved. Materialised here: C1 (5) + A0 x3 (15) + A5 (5) + P (5) + A1 (5) + A2 (5) + A4 (5) = 45 prompts. Executed under §A2.2: steps 0-4 cost 30 calls, step 5 costs 5-15 (it stops at the first arm that matches), so the executable range is 35 minimum and 45 maximum. A3 and C2 are declared and NOT RUN.
note: Order is the registration's frozen order (Amendment 2 §A2.7): C1 -> A0 x3 -> A5 -> P -> M(A1) -> L(A2) -> X(A4) -> N. C1 is first because the batch-validity control must fail before any arm is read (objection 9). Repetitions are laid out outermost (see planRunsFromPlan): all conditions are drawn once, then A0's second and third draws follow, so no two identical prompts are ever adjacent (objection 19). Every brief is a registered string: B1/B3 verbatim from the frozen BRIEFS constant, B3P verbatim from REGISTERED_B3P (Amendment 2 §A2.4). A3 and C2 carry a 'status' of 'not-run' and are refused by the plan loader, never silently included.

conditions.notRunReason: Amendment 2 §A2.3 — S (picker size) is withdrawn and A3 is not run. Measured: A0 -> A3 adds two modes and +242 picker bytes with the owner's position unchanged, while the contrast A3 was built to model (A0 -> A5) adds two modes, removes 536 bytes and moves the owner seven lines. A3 models neither component, so it is untested rather than refuting. The fixture is retained for a future registration that pads both pickers to a common size.
